chapter_theme: Bindu is both the cosmic seed, from which with nada the tattvas, the powers of speech and the worlds unfold as Mahamaya, and the bodily seed, distilled from food through the seven bodily elements. The Lord stands in the seed as a sprout in its seed; those who do not know how bindu is lost, or how to guard it, perish with the perishing body.
structure_note: The chapter moves from bindu as cosmic source (1923 to 1930), through the seed and sprout image for the Lord in the world (1931, 1932), to bindu in the body: its making from food (1933, 1934), its becoming mind (1935) and its loss (1936).

1923.reading: From bindu as it arises come kundalini and, in order, the nine bindu-born powers, the gods beginning with Brahma, the shaktis, the instruments, the kalas and speech.
1923.nuance: குடில் (kutila, the curved one), வயிந்தவம் (baindava, born of bindu), கரணம் and கலை are technical terms of Saiva cosmology, and கலைவை கரியே is taken as கலை, வைகரி (the spoken level of speech). The list order is the tradition's and the verse is compressed.

1924.reading: The distinctions of bindu give twenty-five, those of nada six, and the rest come in twos and twos; together they make the thirty-six tattvas.
1924.nuance: ஐ ஐந்தும் (five fives), ஆறும் (six) and ஈர்இரண்டில் (two twos) do not simply add to ஆறுஆறு (six sixes, 36) as read here; the grouping may be different, or a number may have dropped. The standard Siddhanta count is 36 tattvas.

1925.reading: All the distinctions that arise rest above the supreme bindu; Mahamaya, the goddess of speech, the supreme power and kundalini with kutila, these four shine within bindu.
1925.nuance: மாமாயை, வாகேசி, தற்பரை and குண்டலி are traditionally taken as names of bindu or of powers in it. Whether குடிலை is a fifth name or one with குண்டலி is unclear.

1926.reading: The kalas beginning with nivritti, the letters A and U and M with bindu within M, and the spotless end of nada reached in the eye extend through the mind and its faculties to their end.
1926.nuance: அகர, உகாரம், மகாரம் with விந்து and நாதாந்தம் are the parts of the syllable Om as analysed in mantra theory. கண்ணினுள் (in the eye) and மனாதியுள் அந்தமும் are obscure.

1927.reading: As end and beginning, the Supreme who pervades all is the seed, the root of cause and effect, and performs the five acts.
1927.nuance: வீயம் (seed, bija) and கந்தம் (root, bulb) can be read of the Lord or of bindu as his instrument; the verse runs them together. ஐங்கருமம் are traditionally creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment and grace.

1928.reading: By the power of bindu, which is the seed, the undivided and the cosmos spread out; when the five elements of the body arise in maya as effect, bindu is both inside and outside.
1928.nuance: அகண்டம் (the undivided) and காரிய மாயை (maya as effect) are technical. The verse links cosmic and bodily bindu, which the chapter later treats as one.

1929.reading: Bindu enters and shines through everything within and without; its colour is white and nada's red, and joined with Shakti and Siva it has power over life and grants release.
1929.nuance: White bindu and red nada are traditionally matched with Siva and Shakti and, in the body, with semen and female blood. சிவபாதம் and ஆயுள் may also be taken as Siva's feet and length of life.

1930.reading: This bindu, flawless like the Supreme, stays in its effects as thread stays in cloth and clay in a pot, and as cause and effect of the kalas and the rest becomes all the worlds: it is Mahamaya.
1930.nuance: படம், கடம் (cloth, pot) are the classic examples of a material cause present in its effect. The verse makes bindu the material cause of the worlds, distinct from the Supreme it resembles.

1931.reading: Nandi stands in that seed and is sweet there, but people do not perceive how he is in this seed; the holy one stands in the seed common to all, as flower and swan in the seed of honey.
1931.nuance: The play on வித்து (seed) runs through every line. மதுவித்திலே மலர் அன்னம் அதாகி is obscure: மலர் and அன்னம் may be the lotus and swan of Brahma, or அன்னம் may mean food. The plain sense is that the Lord is in the seed of things unseen.

1932.reading: There is no sprout without the seed, no way for the sprout to appear except from the seed, and seed and sprout exist only together; those who see this see Hara's way.
1932.nuance: The verse does not say what seed and sprout stand for. They are commonly taken as Siva and the world, or Siva and Shakti: cause and effect inseparable. Placed here, it may also bear on bodily bindu and the body.

1933.reading: Food eaten divides into three parts, the body's, the mind's and the waste that leaves; the body's and the mind's parts join, and what was there before becomes chyle.
1933.nuance: The threefold division of food into body, mind and waste is an old physiological teaching. இருந்தன முன்னாள் is unclear: perhaps what lay in the stomach the day before.

1934.reading: Of the seven bodily elements beginning with chyle, each forming in three days, a rare drop of bindu arises like dew on a single blade of grass, and over seven threes of days the gathered bindu grows in the body.
1934.nuance: ஏழ் மூன்றின் is read as seven times three, twenty-one days. The dew on a grass blade marks smallness and rarity. Sengalvaraya notes a parallel in Tiruppugazh 862, where a drop like dew on a grass tip grows into a body.

1935.reading: Within three days it mingles in the body and the kala-bindu becomes one's own mind; for those who hold steady it is not lost, but those who follow illusion perish with their mind.
1935.nuance: கலாவிந்து and நேயத்தே நின்றோர் (those who stand in love, or in what is fitting) are unclear. The claim that bindu becomes mind ties bodily continence to mental steadiness, as tradition reads it.

1936.reading: People do not know how much bindu is being lost, nor how to guard within themselves what is leaving; worn out in a perishing body, they perish, knowing the perishing yet not stopping it.
1936.nuance: அழி (perish) opens three lines and the last, so the verse sounds what it describes. அறிந்தொழியாரே can mean 'they do not know and desist' or 'they do not stop though they know'. Unlike the poets who answer the body's perishing by turning from it, Tirumular calls for guarding it.

links.note: The chapter's two bindus: the cosmic one from which kundalini, gods and speech unfold (1923), and the drop distilled from food in the body (1934). Tirumular gives both the same name and the same generative role.
1931 says the Lord is in the seed unperceived; 1932 states the logic: no sprout apart from its seed, and seed and sprout only together.

Both use dew on a grass blade. The Naladiyar makes it the body's brief life and urges good deeds now; Tirumular makes it the rare drop of bindu from which the body's strength grows, something to be kept rather than a reminder of loss.
724 says that if the body perishes the life perishes, and that Tirumular learned how to nourish the body; 1936 names one way it perishes, the unguarded loss of bindu.

Both start from the perishing body. The Naladiyar's wise see it as a bubble and resolve to end their births; Tirumular faults people for not guarding what keeps the body. The facts agree, the response differs.

source_issues: 1924: the numbers (25, 6, two twos) do not obviously total the stated 36; the grouping or a number may be lost.
1923 line 4 (கலைவை கரியே) and 1931 line 3 (மதுவித்திலே மலர் அன்னம்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
